Game

new Game([options])

Everything a point-and-click game needs, wired together with sensible defaults: rooms, a hero, hotspots, an inventory, scripts, cutscenes, dialogue, saving and sound.

In a sketch you get one from createGame. new Game(options) makes the same object without p5, for tests or for a game's logic in its own module.

Example

const game = createGame({
  rooms: [{
    id: 'yard', width: 640, height: 360, color: '#2d3a55',
    starts: { default: { x: 80, y: 300 } },
    walkable: [{ id: 'floor', points: [[0, 250], [640, 250], [640, 340], [0, 340]] }],
  }],
});
await game.start();
ParameterTypeMeaning
optionsGameOptionsoptionalSee GameOptions.

Properties

debug

game.debug boolean

Shows the outlines of hotspots and floors while true. The debugKey (default d) toggles it.

actors

game.actors Array.<{baseline: number, draw: function(Object): void}>

Extra things drawn in depth order with the hero: objects with a baseline (the y of their feet) and a draw(p) function.

scaler

game.scaler LetterboxScaler | undefined

Fits the canvas to the window with letterbox bars. Set when the game is attached to p5.

options

game.options GameOptions

The options the game was made with, defaults filled in.

core

game.core Object

The pieces createCore() makes (events, state, scheduler, text, game loop), kept together.

events

game.events EventBus

The event bus: game.events.on('room:enter', fn).

state

game.state StateStore

The game's memory: flags, variables, inventory, the current room. Saved by save().

scheduler

game.scheduler Scheduler

Game-time timers: await game.scheduler.wait(1000). They stop while the game is paused.

i18n

game.i18n I18n

Text keys and translations: game.i18n.t('sign.look').

rooms

game.rooms Map.<string, Object>

The rooms by id.

scene

game.scene SceneManager

Moves between rooms; also holds the camera (game.scene.camera).

hero

game.hero Actor

The player's character: await game.hero.walkTo({ x: 300, y: 300 }).

hover

game.hover HoverTracker

Finds the hotspot under the pointer.

inventory

game.inventory Inventory

What the player carries.

settings

game.settings Settings

The player's settings: text speed, subtitles, volumes. Saved separately from the game.

subtitles

game.subtitles SubtitleBar

The bar that shows the lines being said.

menu

game.menu ChoiceMenu

The menu of dialogue choices.

dialogue

game.dialogue DialogueSession

Plays conversations (see Game#talk).

cutscenes

game.cutscenes Cutscenes

Runs cutscenes (see Game#cutscene).

audio

game.audio AudioManager | null

Music and sound effects; null when the game has no sounds.

interactor

game.interactor Interactor

Turns clicks into actions and runs the scripts.

scripts

game.scripts Scripts

The registry of scripts (see Game#on).

bar

game.bar InventoryBar

The inventory bar at the bottom of the screen.

pointer

game.pointer PointerController

Mouse and touch behaviour (click, long press, tap to highlight).

room

game.room Object | undefined

The room the hero is in, or undefined before Game#start.

Methods

addRoom

game.addRoom(source)

Adds a room after the game was made. A URL is fetched by Game#start.

ParameterTypeMeaning
sourceObject | stringA room object, or the URL of a room JSON file.

Returns Game The game, so calls can be chained.

Example

game.addRoom({ id: 'cellar', width: 640, height: 360, color: '#222', starts: { default: { x: 100, y: 300 } }, walkable: [] });

on

game.on(id, handlers)

Sets what happens when the player acts on a hotspot, an item or a room. A handler gets a context ctx with ctx.say(key), ctx.hero, ctx.inventory, ctx.state, ctx.item and ctx.setEnabled(id, on). Returning false from a handler gives the default answer.

ParameterTypeMeaning
idstringThe id of a hotspot, an item or a room.
handlersObjectAny of onInteract (click), onLook (right-click or long press), onUse (an item was used on it), onEnter (a room, screen still black), onEntered (a room, after the fade-in) and onExit.

Returns Game The game, so calls can be chained.

Example

game.on('door', {
  onLook: (ctx) => ctx.say('door.look'),
  onUse: async (ctx) => {
    if (ctx.item !== 'key') return false;
    ctx.inventory.remove('key');
    game.flag('doorOpen', true);
    await ctx.say('door.opens');
  },
});

preload

game.preload()

Loads room files, pictures and sounds once. Game#start calls it for you; call it yourself to load while a title screen shows.

Returns Promise.<void>

start

game.start([roomId], [startName])

Loads everything the game needs, then enters a room.

ParameterTypeMeaning
roomIdstringoptionalThe room to start in. Default: the first one added.
startNamestringoptional (default 'default')Which of the room's starts the hero appears at.

Returns Promise.<void> Resolves once the room is entered.

Example

async function setup() {
  game = createGame({ rooms: [yard] });
  await game.start();
}

goTo

game.goTo(roomId, [startName])

Changes room with a fade. The state remembers each room, so it is as you left it when you come back.

ParameterTypeMeaning
roomIdstringThe room to go to.
startNamestringoptional (default 'default')Which of that room's starts the hero appears at.

Returns Promise.<void> Resolves when the new room has faded in. Throws if a change is already running.

Example

game.on('door', { onInteract: () => game.goTo('hall', 'fromYard') });

say

game.say(key, [options])

The hero says a line. Everything the player reads is a text key from strings; a key that is missing shows as [key], which is easy to spot.

ParameterTypeMeaning
keystringA text key, such as 'sign.look'.
optionsObjectoptionalPassed to Actor#say.

Returns Promise.<void> Resolves when the line is over (or the player skips it).

Example

await game.say('sign.look');

talk

game.talk(source, [options])

Plays a conversation. The format is detected: Markdown text, Twee 3 text (starts with ::), Twison JSON, compiled Ink JSON or an inkjs Story, or a ready-made dialogue runner. Ink variables are saved with the game, and Ink can call giveItem("key") and setFlag("name").

ParameterTypeMeaning
sourcestring | ObjectThe conversation.
optionsObjectoptional
options.syncArray.<string>optionalInk only: which variables to keep in the state (default: all).
options.externalsObject.<string, function()>optionalInk only: extra EXTERNAL functions.
options.startstringoptionalMarkdown only: the section to begin with.

Returns Promise.<void> Resolves when the conversation ends.

Example

await game.talk(`
# start
Guard: Halt! Who goes there?
* Just me -> me
* A friend -> friend

# me
Guard: Move along, then.
-> END

# friend
Guard: Any friend of the lighthouse is a friend of mine.
-> END
`);

cutscene

game.cutscene(script, [options])

Runs a cutscene: the player cannot act, and a Skip button (or Escape) ends it early, jumping the hero and the fade to where they would have ended up. The script's state changes still happen, so a skipped cutscene ends in the same state as a played one.

ParameterTypeMeaning
scriptfunctionAn async function. It gets the cutscene controller cs; cs.label('name') marks a place that skip('name') can stop at.
optionsObjectoptional
options.skippablebooleanoptional (default true)false hides the Skip button.

Returns Promise.<*> Resolves with the script's result when it ends or is skipped.

Example

await game.cutscene(async () => {
  await game.hero.walkTo({ x: 300, y: 300 });
  await game.say('intro.hello');
});

flag

game.flag(name, [value])

Reads or sets a yes/no fact about the game. Flags are saved with the game.

ParameterTypeMeaning
namestringThe flag's name. Do not put dots in it.
valuebooleanoptionalGiven: the flag is set to it. Left out: the flag is read.

Returns boolean The flag's value (false if it was never set).

Example

if (!game.flag('doorOpen')) await game.say('door.locked');
game.flag('doorOpen', true);

give

game.give(item)

Puts an item in the inventory.

ParameterTypeMeaning
itemstringAn id from the items option.

Returns boolean true, or false if it was already carried.

Example

game.give('key');

take

game.take(item)

Removes an item from the inventory.

ParameterTypeMeaning
itemstringAn id from the items option.

Returns boolean true, or false if it was not carried.

has

game.has(item)

Asks whether an item is carried.

ParameterTypeMeaning
itemstringAn id from the items option.

Returns boolean

Example

if (game.has('key')) await game.say('door.unlock');

hotspot

game.hotspot(id)

The live hotspot of the current room, for example to switch it off with .enabled = false.

ParameterTypeMeaning
idstringThe hotspot's id.

Returns Hotspot | null null if the current room has no such hotspot.

update

game.update(dt)

Moves the game forward one step. With createGame, p5 calls this every frame, so you only call it yourself in tests or in a game without p5.

ParameterTypeMeaning
dtnumberMilliseconds since the last step. Capped at 100.

save

game.save([slot])

Saves the game: the state (flags, inventory, current room) and where the hero stands.

ParameterTypeMeaning
slotstringoptionalDefault: the saveSlot option.

Example

game.save();

load

game.load([slot])

Loads a saved game and re-enters its room.

ParameterTypeMeaning
slotstringoptionalDefault: the saveSlot option.

Returns Promise.<boolean> false when nothing is saved in that slot.

Example

if (!(await game.load())) await game.start();

draw

game.draw()

Draws everything: the room, the hero, subtitles, choices, the inventory bar, hover label and fades. Call it in draw(). Added to the game by createGame.

Example

function draw() {
  game.draw();
}

drawRoom

game.drawRoom(p, room, game)

Draws the room's floors, obstacles and hotspots in room coordinates. Replace it to draw your own art; the default is drawRoomShapes, so a replacement can call it and add to it.

ParameterTypeMeaning
pObjectThe p5 sketch.
roomObjectThe current room.
gameGame

Example

game.drawRoom = (p, room, game) => {
  p.background(30, 40, 60);
  p5.clickery.drawRoomShapes(p, room, game);
};

drawHero

game.drawHero(p, hero, game)

Draws the hero, feet at (hero.x, hero.y). Replace it to draw your own character; the default is drawHeroDefault.

ParameterTypeMeaning
pObjectThe p5 sketch.
heroActor
gameGame

drawSpeech

game.drawSpeech(p, hero, game)

Draws the line the hero is saying, while there is one. The default is drawSpeechDefault.

ParameterTypeMeaning
pObjectThe p5 sketch.
heroActor
gameGame
